Remember that ironic get_user_pages race?  when the raised page_count on a
page swapped out led do_wp_page to decide that it had to copy on write
substituted a different page into userspace.  2.6.7 onwards have Andrea's
solution
column2: where try_to_unmap_one backs out if it finds page_count raised.

column1: Which works
column2: but is unsatisfying (rmap.c has no other page_count heuristics)

column1: and was found a few months ago to hang an intensive page migration test.  A
year ago I was hesitant to engage page_mapcount
column2: now it seems the right fix.

column1: So remove the page_count hack from try_to_unmap_one; and use activate_page in
unuse_mm when dropping lock
column2: to replace its secondary effect of helping

column1: swapoff to make progress in that case.
Simplify can_share_swap_page (now called only on anonymous pages) to check
page_mapcount + page_swapcount == 1: still needs the page lock to stabilize
their (pessimistic) sum
column2: but does not need swapper_space.tree_lock for that.

column1: In do_swap_page
column2: move swap_free and unlock_page below page_add_anon_rmap

column1: keep sum on the high side
